hook_text: In 1808, a tailor in a borrowed uniform led three hundred people towards Cape Town to demand their freedom.
clip_script: October 1808. Louis of Mauritius, an enslaved tailor, puts on a borrowed uniform and rides into the Swartland. Farm by farm, he and his allies tie up the owners, take their horses and guns, and call enslaved people and Khoikhoi workers to join them. Nobody is killed. More than three hundred people march towards Cape Town, demanding freedom. At Salt River, British soldiers are waiting. The rebellion ends without a battle, and Louis and four others are hanged. But the message was clear: enslaved people never accepted slavery.
visual_style: A night ride across wheat fields, a growing column of people, then cavalry silhouettes at a river crossing; a final title card with the year 1834.
mood: Tense and dramatic, ending with dignity.
pacing: Building momentum, a sudden stop at the river, a quiet close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on slave resistance at the Cape.
